question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, Regulation 23, how frequently must Category I and Category II AIFs undertake valuation of their investments by an independent valuer, and under what condition can this period be extended?

answer.text: Once every 3 months by default; extendable to 6 months with 51% investor approval by value
Once every year by default; extendable to 2 years with 50% investor approval by number
Once every 6 months by default; extendable to 1 year with 75% investor approval by value of investment
Once every 6 months by default; extendable to 1 year with unanimous investor approval

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (pages 421-422) and Regulation 23(2), Cat I and Cat II AIFs must value their investments at least once every six months by an independent valuer; this period can be extended to one year with the approval of at least 75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF. The Trap: A 3-month frequency is not the Regulation 23 default. A 1-year default is not the regulation. Unanimous approval is too strict; the regulation uses a 75%-by-value threshold, not headcount. Note: The six-month frequency and 75%-by-value extension are stated in pages 421-422; the six-month valuation cadence is repeated in the compliance table on page 433.
